sentences.span: the 10yr yield (+12.2bps) rose to 4.96%, the highest since October 2023
sentences.why: Exact figure and comparison period match DB's Reid note.

sentences.span: Yet again, the main driver was a big jump in energy prices, with Brent crude surging above $107/bbl
sentences.why: Opinion-shaped transition sentence, but it restates the source's own causal framing that energy was the day's main driver.

sentences.span: Brent crude (+6.34%) ended the session at $107.63/bbl... futures raised the probability of a September hike from 60% on Wednesday to 72%
sentences.why: All three clauses (Brent close, PPI/PCE components 'came in on the stronger side', hike-odds move 60%->72%) appear verbatim in the same DB note.

sentences.span: US Treasury bought back $5.19bn of long-dated debt, falling short of the $6bn maximum it had announced on Wednesday
sentences.why: Figures match exactly; the same note shows 2yr/10yr/30yr yields all rising that session, supporting 'yields rose across the curve anyway.'

sentences.span: If nominal GDP settles at 5.5% then 4.8% would be historically average. If we settle at 6% due to AI and inflation, then around 5.3% is reasonable
sentences.why: Deutsche Bank chartbook gives 6.6% spot nominal GDP and the identical 4.8%/5.3% scenario figures, and elsewhere calls the yield rise 'a continuation of a long normalisation process.'

sentences.span: for core, they expect a relatively softer +0.21% monthly print... (CPI - Core // 0.21% // 0.20% // 0.20%)
sentences.why: Deutsche Bank's own core CPI forecast is 0.21%, matching the sentence.

sentences.span: We expect a 0.23% increase in August core CPI (vs. +0.2% consensus)
sentences.why: Goldman's desk note gives exactly 0.23% vs 0.2% consensus.

sentences.span: the hyperscaler complex will issue MORE DV01 than the US Treasury... If investors purchase hyperscaler bonds by reducing Treasury or mortgage exposure, the effect can spill into government yields
sentences.why: DV01 = interest-rate exposure; the transcript also ties the buyer-substitution mechanism to credit spreads and term premium ('higher real yields and a fatter term premium are the clearing mechanism').

sentences.span: Mark Wilson's recently comments that, "The Fed are much more passenger than driver in this debate."
short term CTA thresholds across all three indices (ndx, spx, rty) have broken this morning... in addition to european index which broke down earlier in the week
sentences.why: CTA = trend-following funds; ndx/spx/rty = Nasdaq 100/S&P 500/Russell 2000; note is timestamped Thu 10 Sep 2026, 9:23am ET.

sentences.span: those 'in-the-know' believe market bets on three additional hikes "may be too aggressive."
sentences.why: The 'no brainer' quote is faithful, but no source shows money markets 'fully' pricing three more ECB hikes: the only three-hikes figure is a hedged trader bet the source itself calls possibly 'too aggressive'. The confident 'fully price' language instead belongs to the Fed's separately-tracked path in the same DB note ('at least 3 hikes are fully priced in over the next year'), so the sentence appears to misattribute Fed hike-pricing certainty to the ECB.

sentences.span: TSMC is adding further N3 capacity and still does not expect supply to be sufficient... CoWoS capacity remains tight, and TSMC already started outsourcing selected packaging processes to OSAT partners
sentences.why: N3 = 3-nanometer; source explicitly contrasts this with prior nodes where demand faded two to three years post-introduction, and confirms the OSAT outsourcing detail.

sentences.span: Bottom line: stay long AI infra as scarcity across compute & energy remains a theme well into 2027
sentences.why: 'Stay long AI infra into 2027' is a real GS desk bottom line, but no source contains a 'buy its AI hardware basket' call — the only AI Hardware basket reference in the day's set is GS Prime positioning data (long/short ratio at the 51st percentile), not a recommendation. The sentence bolts an invented specific call onto a real one.

sentences.span: 'bottoms up' datapoints remain very constructive... juxtaposed against lingering 'top down' debates – an output of Summer volatility, macro uncertainty (Rates, geopolitical), policy uncertainty (midterms)
sentences.why: Directly supports the framing that company-level ('bottoms up') data is fine while top-down rates/geopolitics/midterm-policy concerns are what's holding stocks back.

sentences.span: Forward earnings, revenues and margins have been driving tech stocks higher this year. Forward P/Es, however, have slumped
sentences.why: Near-verbatim match for the valuation-divergence claim.
